A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiTrajDiff work. All 17 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original D4RL experiments across four offline RL backbones, together with direction, filtering, augmentation-ratio and n-step analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains the D4RL experiments and adds original two-room toy-task and OGBench results, including goal-conditioned evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the specified return-conditioning inputs from finite H-dependent windows to full discounted future/history sums. The diffusion architecture, anchor stitching, completion models and filters remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this specification change involved implementation changes or reruns.

E1.justification: v5 adds a two-room scenario with no cross-door training trajectories and OGBench evaluations covering antmaze, humanoidmaze and cube manipulation. Tables S4-S5 introduce single-task and goal-conditioned stitching/exploration coverage. The earlier D4RL coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The D4RL comparator set remains Synther, DiffStitch and RTDiff. New OGBench comparisons evaluate ASTRO and SSD alongside Synther/DiffStitch for single-task RL, and SCoTS/CD alongside Synther for goal-conditioned RL. The toy comparison additionally evaluates the trajectory-level Synther-long variant against RTDiff and BiTrajDiff.

E3.justification: v5 adds evaluation configurations using FQL and backbones labeled GCIQL/CRL, plus cross-door success evaluation with IQL/TD3BC. Section 5.5 changes the stated dynamic-error metric from summed L2 norms to summed squared L2 norms, without establishing recalculation. Existing D4RL training budgets, horizon, augmentation ratio and n-step settings are retained; detailed protocols for the new evaluations are sparse.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a didactic failure-case analysis testing whether generation bridges two disconnected trajectory groups despite state coverage near their doorway. The existing direction, filter, augmentation-ratio, n-step and accuracy/diversity analyses remain, with appendix renumbering and limited numerical or definitional corrections.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and S2 retain five-seed standard-deviation reporting. New OGBench Table S4 uses mixed reporting: Base, ASTRO, DiffStitch and Synther have point estimates, while SSD and BiTrajDiff have accompanying uncertainty values. The new experiments lack an explicit run-count specification. Changed uncertainty values in retained results do not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: v5 adds toy-task findings and OGBench results, including BiTrajDiff averages of 63.0/74.7 for IQL/FQL and 21.7/33.7 for GCIQL/CRL. Tables 1-2 retain task-level scores but revise aggregates, such as the Table 1 IQL baseline average from 77.5 to 79.1. Appendix Tables S2-S3 revise numerous entries: DT DiffStitch on walker2d-medium changes from 77.8±4.0 to 72.3±9.4. These are reported numerical revisions, not demonstrated performance changes from rerunning an unchanged setting.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the forward-return summation upper bound from t+H to infinity and the backward-return lower bound from t-H to zero. Section 5.5 changes dynamic error from an L2 norm to a squared L2 norm, while retaining the squared-error prose. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: Global connectivity, bidirectional stitching and improved offline RL performance were already central claims in v3. v5 replaces the explicit first-to-explore future/history contribution with identifying a connectivity limitation of single-rollout methods, and extends its contrast to backward-only approaches. This refines the novelty framing while retaining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly distinguishes coverage of states near the doorway from connectivity of complete trajectories, interpreting failed single-direction generation as preservation of dataset connectivity. Appendix D interprets OGBench gains as evidence of compositional recovery. Earlier explanations concerning filtering, synthetic-data noise and n-step estimation errors remain.

D1.justification: v3's explicit statement that implementation code is supplied in supplementary material is removed. v5 retains only the promise of public release upon publication. Appendix B otherwise preserves the architecture, hardware, optimizer, training budget, sampling and filtering details.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion now acknowledges backward-history methods instead of characterizing existing augmentation as forward-only. It adds GTA and references supporting OGBench, FQL and the ASTRO/SSD/SCoTS/CD comparisons. This is a focused expansion and correction; most of the literature review and its organization remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around connectivity, the boxed research question disappears, and contributions become bullets. Experimental prose and the conclusion are shortened or revised. The ethics statement becomes an impact statement, the reproducibility and LLM-use sections disappear, and author, affiliation and header text changes.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column ICLR layout to a two-column ICML layout, substantially reflowing displays. v5 adds the two-room Figure 1 and OGBench Tables S4-S5, rearranges the n-step figure from four horizontal panels to a 2×2 grid, and reformats v3's numerical Figure S1 as Table S9.

improvement.justification: v5 gives the existing connectivity claim more targeted support through the two-room demonstration and OGBench comparisons with additional stitching methods, while correcting verifiable aggregation errors in Tables 1 and S2. These improve evidential relevance and numerical consistency. Benefits are limited by sparse protocols and uneven uncertainty reporting for new experiments, removal of the supplementary-code disclosure, and an introduced reversal of initial/terminal conditioning in the introduction that contradicts Section 4.1.
